children: shares dropped 2% in Friday morning trading as UBS cut its price target on the AI computing company to $105 from $120, while keeping its Buy recommendation.

The revised target reflects concerns about financing conditions and investor sentiment rather than a newly identified weakness in the company's operations. UBS analyst Karl Keirstead said demand trends, GPU pricing and CoreWeave's expansion into additional services remain supportive of its business outlook.

CoreWeave faces particular pressure when markets become less receptive to companies that need large amounts of capital. Building AI data centers requires substantial spending, while the company's negative free cash flow and reliance on debt make its valuation more sensitive to higher interest rates.

The stock's decline also comes amid broader uncertainty over how much companies will continue spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. UBS views that wider reassessment as a key factor weighing on heavily funded AI businesses, rather than evidence that CoreWeave's own business prospects have suddenly weakened.

Although the bank retained its positive rating, the lower price target signals a more cautious view of the stock's near-term potential. Keirstead indicated that a recovery in investor confidence could take time as markets reassess AI investment and financing risks.

title: CoreWeave Stock Falls After UBS Cuts Price Target on AI Spending
